Class IuJsonProperties

java.lang.Object
edu.iu.client.IuJsonProperties
public final class IuJsonProperties extends Object
Indexes the properties of one JSON object, converting each to Java only when it's read.

A property resolves from the first of three places that has it:

  1. Values already resolved, which a read returns directly.
  2. Raw JsonValues, from a JsonObject or captured from a parser, which convert on first read.
  3. A parser inside the object. A read pulls forward: the property it asks for converts straight from the parser, with no tree built, and properties passed on the way are captured raw, needing no type and no conversion.

An index reading from a parser must detach() before whatever controls the parser moves on; within a JSON-B deserialization by the IU JSON-B provider, the provider detaches it. Detaching from a parser over text the provider holds keeps reading the rest of the object from that text, in place, and releases the text once the object is read through; otherwise the rest is captured raw. Until detached, an index reading from a parser belongs to the parser's thread; otherwise it is thread-safe.

A property the reader never asks for is kept raw and written back unchanged; requireOnly(Set) checks for unexpected ones. The index is immutable: builder() creates one from Java values, and with(String, Object) copies one with a value replaced.

An index converts by the conversions it's created with, or, created without them, by the first of:

  1. the IU JSON-B provider's call in progress when it converts, so values an application indexes and passes to Jsonb.toJson(Object), or writes from a serializer, convert by that call's configuration;
  2. the provider's call in progress when the index was created, so an index a deserializer creates converts that way after the call returns;
  3. the JSON-B instance given to builder(Jsonb), if built with one; else the IU conversions, as IuJsonAdapter.adapt(Type, java.util.function.Supplier) converts with IuJsonSerializationOptions.DEFAULT.

An index is itself a value both the IU conversions and the IU JSON-B provider convert, with nothing to register: written as the object it indexes, and read as an index of the object, as a top-level value, a property, or an item. Read by IuJsonAdapter.adapt(Type, java.util.function.Supplier), it converts as that adapter's value types do; read by JSON-B, as described above.

The same index may so convert differently in different calls. A serializer running under any JSON-B provider can write an index through the call's context with write(JsonGenerator, jakarta.json.bind.serializer.SerializationContext).

    • read

      public static IuJsonProperties read(JsonParser parser, Function<Type, IuJsonAdapter<?>> adapt)
      Indexes an object as a parser reads it.

      An object already in memory, as in a JSON-B tree conversion, is referenced rather than read. Otherwise the index reads from the parser, which it leaves between properties; call detach() before advancing the parser past the object, unless the parser is one the IU JSON-B provider gave a deserializer, which detaches the index itself.

      Parameters:
      parser - parser, at the object's START_OBJECT
      adapt - gets the conversion for a type
      Returns:
      IuJsonProperties
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the parser isn't at an object

    • builder

      public static IuJsonProperties.Builder builder(jakarta.json.bind.Jsonb jsonb)
      Starts building an index from Java values, converting as the JSON-B call in progress converts, and otherwise as a JSON-B instance does.

      Where no call is in progress, as when a value put as one type is read as another, as BigInteger put and byte[] read, the instance's configuration applies, its adapters included, in place of the IU defaults. An instance of the IU JSON-B provider converts directly; one of another provider converts through JSON text.

      Parameters:
      jsonb - JSON-B instance to convert as when no call is in progress
      Returns:
      IuJsonProperties.Builder
      See Also:
      • IuJsonProperties

    • detach

      public void detach()
      Releases the parser the index reads from, so whatever controls it can move on.

      From a parser over text the IU JSON-B provider holds, the index keeps reading the rest of the object from that text, in place, releasing it once the object is read through. From any other parser it captures the rest raw now. Either way the parser is left at the object's END_OBJECT, or where a provider can skip to it. Does nothing if already detached.

    • write

      public void write(JsonGenerator generator, jakarta.json.bind.serializer.SerializationContext context)
      Writes the object from a JSON-B serializer, converting each Java value through the serialization context, as its runtime type, so the call's configuration applies with any JSON-B provider.

      A property read as JSON writes back unchanged; one set to a Java null is written as the context writes a null property, so omitted unless the call writes null properties. The index is read through first.

      Parameters:
      generator - generator the serializer was given, where a value is expected
      context - serialization context
